articles.headline: Eagles look to add to perfect start by stopping the Bears' rushing attack on Monday night
articles.description: — The Chicago Bears made a memorable trip to Philadelphia in November, rushing for 281 yards in an impressive 24-15 victory over the Eagles.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- — The Chicago Bears made a memorable trip to Philadelphia in November, rushing for 281 yards in an impressive 24-15 victory over the Eagles.


              Philadelphia is hoping to return the favor on Monday night, when it visits Chicago in search of a second straight road win.


              “They are one of the better running teams in the league,” Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said. “They’ve got a really great (offensive line), great backs. Their scheme is good. We’re going to have to play it a whole lot better.”


              It would be difficult to play it any worse than they did in their matchup last season. D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai both went over 100 yards rushing as Chicago possessed the ball for almost 40 minutes in its fifth consecutive victory — a streak that helped propel the Bears to the NFC North title. Philadelphia gained just 87 yards on the ground in the loss.


              Swift and Monangai led the way again as Chicago rushed for 291 yards in this year's season opener at Carolina on Sept. 13. But the Bears' ground game was held in check during Sunday's 9-3 loss to Minnesota, finishing with 134 yards on 31 attempts.


              Chicago has an uncertain situation at quarterback with Caleb Williams dealing with a right hamstring injury and Tyson Bagent in the concussion protocol. But Fangio doesn't think it will have much of an effect on the Bears' rushing scheme.


              “They’re an under-center offense a good bit, so it’s not like it’s a lot of gun zone-read, QB-generated runs,” Fangio said. “They’re under center, handing it off. They do a great job of blocking.”


              Philadelphia is coming off a dramatic 24-20 victory at Tennessee. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with 9 seconds left.


              “It’s a really good team coming in. ... They make it really difficult for you and it’s sound, both sides of the ball,” Bears coach Ben Johnson said. “Special teams a good unit as well, so we’ll have our work cut out for us.”


              If Williams and Bagent are unable to play, Case Keenum is expected to start for Chicago. The 38-year-old Keenum has made 66 starts in 80 career games, but he hasn’t thrown a pass in a regular-season game since Dec. 24, 2023, for Houston against Cleveland.


              “I feel really good,” Keenum said. “There have been some things every year. I call it a little puzzle of trying to figure out how to get your body in the best shape that it can. This year worked a little more on my diet and what I put in, what I fuel it with. Which is not as fun, it’s just boring, but it does help. So, I feel great.”


              Need to know
              Philadelphia (2-0) at Chicago (1-1).


              When/where to watch: Monday, 8:15 p.m. EDT, ESPN/ABC.


              Latest odds: Eagles by 4 1/2.


              Against the spread: Eagles 0-2, Bears 1-1.


              Last week: E

articles.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan faces another disciple in game against Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur
articles.description: — San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he might appreciate one day how many assistants that used to work under him have become head coaches in the NFL.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he might appreciate one day how many assistants that used to work under him have become head coaches in the NFL.


              That time sure isn't this week as the 49ers (2-0) prepare to face his former assistant Mike LaFleur for the first time since LaFleur got hired as head coach of the division rival Arizona Cardinals (1-1) at home on Sunday.


              “Deep down probably, yeah, and eventually,” Shanahan said about the pride he feels in seeing his former assistants succeed. "But, it’s more irritation, especially when you have to run into them twice a year.”


              With LaFleur taking over the Cardinals this season, all three of San Francisco's NFC West rivals are running offenses derived from Shanahan's scheme. Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay worked as an offensive assistant in Washington when Shanahan was offensive coordinator and the Seattle Seahawks hired former Niners tight ends coach Brian Fleury to run their offense.


              That provides the 49ers defense a familiar look, even if it is a challenging one.


              “You talk about just all the movement, all the eye candy,” star linebacker Fred Warner. “You’re having to communicate a ton just to make sure everybody’s on the same page. But the beauty of it is obviously that we’ve gone against that for so long, all training camp. You’re seeing those looks and you’re seeing it from the best of the best, obviously, in our head coach and Brock Purdy.”


              LaFleur worked under Shanahan for seven seasons, first when Shanahan was a coordinator in Cleveland and Atlanta and then for four years after he took over as head coach in San Francisco in 2017.


              He faced him several times the last three seasons when he was offensive coordinator for the Rams but now gets to do it for the first time as a head coach.


              “When you’re in the moment, you’re in the moment,” he said. "You’re not thinking about that stuff. I’m excited to see him before the game obviously and say what’s up, but then it’s on. That’s how they’re going to feel and that’s how we feel. I’m sure when all is said and done next February and we get to see each other in the offseason; we’ll talk about it. (Until then) this is the Niners versus the Cardinals.”


              Need to know
              Arizona (1-1) vs San Francisco (2-0).

              Series record: Cardinals lead 38-31.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Giants' Nabers trending toward playing Sunday
articles.description: Giants wideout Malik Nabers is nursing a shoulder injury but says he should be fine for Sunday's game.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 24: Notes from NFL Nation

  Giants' Nabers (shoulder) trending in right direction for Sunday

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers practiced for a second straight day Thursday and said he's feeling good and should be fine after injuring his shoulder Monday night against the Los Angeles Rams. Nabers looks like he's trending toward playing Sunday against the Tennessee Titans without any playing-time restrictions. An X-ray earlier in the week on Nabers' shoulder didn't reveal any serious problems. "Good results," he said. "I'm smiling. I'm out there playing, catching the ball. So, good results." -- Jordan Raanan

Sept. 23: Need a QB before Week 3? The best reliable, under-the-radar options

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

You couldn't find much more contrast between Weeks 1 and 2 of this NFL season.

A week after the NFL matched the opening-week record for points scored (791), the 32 teams combined to score only 647 in Week 2. Per ESPN Research, the 647 are the fewest points in any non-Week 18 slate since Week 2 of the 2024 season.

Injuries had quite a bit to do with it, particularly at the quarterback position. Through two weeks, we've already seen five starters depart games due to injury, and that excludes the Atlanta Falcons' two combatants for their starting job (Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.) who have yet to play in 2026. Among the quarterbacks expected to be absent for Week 3 are three members of the position's top 10 in terms of ADP (average draft position): Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart and Caleb Williams.

These high-profile injury setbacks have sent many a fantasy manager scrambling to find a quality quarterback, and there are plenty of options out there to be had -- standard, Knockout, Vampire, etc., leagues alike. Three in particular stand out, players who went 17th or later at the position in the preseason but are suddenly viable starters:

Tyler Shough, New Orleans Saints: His Consistency Ratings won't reflect it due to his initial backup status to begin last season, but if we splice Shough's results into the games he started versus served in a backup capacity, he has been remarkably reliable. articles.headline: Bob Pettit, who starred at LSU and then in NBA, dies at 93
articles.description: Bob Pettit, who was named an All-Star in each of his 11 NBA seasons and was one of the greatest scorers and rebounders in league history, has died, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame said Thursday.
articles.body:
Bob Pettit, who was named an All-Star in each of his 11 NBA seasons and was one of the greatest scorers and rebounders in league history, has died, the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame said Thursday.

He was 93.

Pettit was a two-time NBA MVP, winning the award the first time it was given out in 1955-56 and again in 1958-59. He led the league in scoring both seasons, with 25.7 and 29.2 points per game, respectively.

He was a four-time All-Star Game MVP, a feat matched only by Kobe Bryant, for whom that award was named after his death in January 2020.

Pettit led the Hawks to four NBA Finals appearances and a championship in 1958 over the Boston Celtics, with Pettit scoring 50 points in the Game 6 clincher, a playoff record at that time.

Pettit starred for LSU, averaging 31.4 points and 17.3 rebounds per game in his senior season. The forward was drafted second in 1954 by the Milwaukee Hawks -- a year later they moved to St. Louis -- and responded by being named Rookie of the Year with 20.8 points and 13.8 rebounds per game.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Pulisic set to get contract extension at Milan
articles.description: USMNT star Christian Pulisic is reportedly planning to continue his stint at AC Milan. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract, while Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract extending until the summer of 2031, according to Corriere dello Sport. Initial talks have begun with the 28-year-old's representatives over a deal worth around €5 million per season following his goal-scoring performance in Sunday's 3-0 win over Lecce.

- Real Madrid are keeping tabs on Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl, according to Bild's Christian Falk. Los Blancos are among several teams interested in the 18-year-old, with whom the Bundesliga champions plan to open contract renewal talks, while rival clubs monitor whether Michael Olise's presence in his position could create a transfer opportunity. Karl said during an event in January that playing for Madrid would be a "dream" which led to an apology after the comments sparked anger among Bayern fans.

- Chelsea are considering Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Feyenoord's Gjivai Zechiël as potential successors to Enzo Fernández, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old Zechiel has registered five goals and four assists in seven Eredivisie matches this season, attracting interest from Chelsea, Liverpool, and five other Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri is being scouted by Juventus, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The 25-year-old tops the Bianconeri shortlist for the January transfer window, with a loan approach lined up due to his lack of playing time under Enzo Maresca, while RB Leipzig's David Raum is considered an alternative.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are interested in Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae, according to Christian Falk. Both clubs have tracked the 29-year-old South Korea international since the summer, though any move is expected to depend on upcoming contract discussions with the German club.

Other rumors

- Arsenal are among four Premier League teams tracking Sturm Graz midfielder Luca Weinhandl, 17. (TEAMtalk)

- Barcelona sent scouts to watch Athletico Paranaense defender Arthur Dias in their 2-1 victory over Bahia on Sunday. (Sport)

- Bayern Munich are not considering a move for Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade, who is currently on loan at Juventus, despite recent reports. (Christian Falk)

articles.headline: Presti not expecting Thunder downturn despite departures
articles.description: Oklahoma City GM Sam Presti said the Thunder could be as good as past teams despite key offseason departures.
articles.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY -- In last season's playoffs, the Oklahoma City Thunder's dreams of repeating as NBA champions dwindled with a string of untimely injuries and then faded altogether in a Game 7 Western Conference Finals loss at home to the San Antonio Spurs.

For the Thunder, an offseason of change followed, namely trading starter Lu Dort and key reserves in Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins -- all cost-saving moves that shrunk the team's payroll by more than $300 million.

"I think the team last year had another level to it," Thunder executive vice president and general manager Sam Presti said Thursday in his annual preseason news conference. "I think we could have got to another level. But I think in due time, like I said earlier, this particular group of players, if we stay healthy, if it has time together, it has a chance to be as good if not better than any of the teams we've had."

Speaking of their championship core of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, 28, Chet Holmgren, 24, and Jalen Williams, 25, Presti later said, "We have three guys, two of which are not even in their prime, that are All-NBA players, and also the other guy that's a back-to-back MVP [Gilgeous-Alexander], and he's only getting better as well in his prime."

Williams played in just 38 games last season because of injuries, including a left hamstring strain that kept him mostly sidelined in the playoffs against the Spurs.

"He looks fantastic," Presti said. "He looks great. He's playing great. We're looking forward to him being himself again."

During an hour-and-a-half session with reporters, Presti praised the key contributions of Dort, Joe and Wiggins while saying it was "certainly disappointing" to lose them. And he said the Thunder will be different after losing players who roughly played a combined 10,000 minutes over the past two seasons.

"We have to give ourselves time to figure out the best way to position this team because those guys played a lot," Presti said. "They were big influences on things. We're going to have to kind of learn a new way, which is healthy."

He also spoke at length about the second apron -- the financial threshold in the NBA's collective bargaining agreement that has helped shape how teams are constructed.

"When people talk about the aprons, everybody is talking about it from a very small point of view because it affects everybody differently based on your starting point and the timeline of your team," he said. "We have a tendency in this world to paint everything with a broad brush or prescribe something based on one person's symptoms. It's like, everyone has got a different experience with these aprons. So I don't think it can be a broad brush."

Added Presti: "For us, the ghost in the machine is the finances, not so much the aprons. I've said that for three years probably.
